title: Where Is Node.js Used? knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Where Is Node.js Used??
options: Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Keep route handlers focused, validate inputs, centralize async errors, and pin/document the framework version.
questions.answer_key: Keep route handlers focused, validate inputs, centralize async errors, and pin/document the framework version.
questions.explanation: Keep route handlers focused, validate inputs, centralize async errors, and pin/document the framework version. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Where Is Node.js Used??
questions.explanation: “Web servers and REST APIs” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Where Is Node.js Used? implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
